title: tsforge — automatic, evidence-based forecasting for R
text:
Give it a series. It validates, diagnoses, backtests a registry of models with rolling-origin validation, selects the empirical winner for this series and horizon under the configured validation procedure, forecasts with intervals, explains, and builds a Markdown/Quarto dashboard with interactive charts.
There is no universal best method — and this package will never claim one.

title: tsforge — automatic, evidence-based forecasting for R
text:
Why tsforge

Evidence, not preference. The winner is the backtest winner. Ties, failures and unavailable models stay visible for audit.
Honest metrics. 13 error metrics plus interval coverage; MAPE is NA whenever actuals contain zeros — never silently computed.
Extensible. register_model() adds your method without touching core.
Light base. Core runs on base R; ETS, GARCH, VAR, Prophet, ML and plotly are optional and capability-probed.

title: tsforge — automatic, evidence-based forecasting for R

title: Getting started
text:
# from a local checkout / tarball
install.packages("tsforge_1.0.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
Optional capabilities unlock more models (each probed at runtime):
install.packages(c("forecast", "prophet", "rugarch", "vars"))
install.packages(c("ranger", "e1071", "glmnet", "xgboost", "plotly"))

title: Getting started
text:
First forecast
library(tsforge)
df <- data.frame(
  date  = seq(as.Date("2021-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 48),
  value = AirPassengers[1:48])

res <- auto_ts(df, "date", "value", horizon = 12, seed = 1)
summary(res)          # ranking, fit stats, residual diagnostics
plot(res)             # history + forecast + intervals
explain_forecast(res) # why this model, in plain language
db <- ts_dashboard(res, interactive = TRUE)
db                    # dashboard.qmd/.md/index.html + plotly widgets

title: Getting started
text:
Modes and metrics
auto_ts(df, "date", "value", horizon = 12,
        mode = "fast",        # fast | balanced | full
        metric = "MAE",       # any of 13 metrics
        validation = "sliding")

text:

  id = "my_model", name = "My model", family = "machine_learning",
  fit = function(y, h, m, ...) list(last = tail(y, 1)),
  predict = function(fit, h, ...) rep(fit$last, h))

title: Method catalog
text: One row per catalogued method. status == "implemented" runs in this release; the rest are schema-ready roadmap entries. Query it live with model_catalog() and available_models().

title: Method catalog
text:
Baselines and smoothing
naive, snaive, drift, mean, median, ses, holt, hw (base R), ETS and auto.arima (optional forecast package).

title: Method catalog
text:
ARIMA and seasonal
ARIMA grid with AICc (stats), auto.arima, TBATS/BATS (forecast), Theta, trend-seasonal regression.

title: Method catalog
text:
Intermittent demand
Croston Croston (1972), SBA Syntetos and Boylan (2005), TSB Teunter, Syntetos, and Babai (2011), ADIDA Nikolopoulos et al. (2011) — all in base R, compared head-to-head.

title: Method catalog
text:
Volatility and multivariate (standalone modules)
sGARCH via analyze_volatility() (fitted only with ARCH evidence; Engle (1982), Bollerslev (1986)) and VAR via var_forecast() with granger_causality() (Sims (1980)).

title: Method catalog
text:
Machine learning and neural
Temporal features + OLS/kNN (base), ridge/lasso/elastic-net (glmnet), random forest (ranger), SVR (e1071), XGBoost Chen and Guestrin (2016), MLP (nnet); LSTM/Transformer et al. probed via dl_capabilities().

title: Method catalog
text:
Selection
Rolling-origin backtest, 13 metrics, configurable primary metric, near-tie detection, residual diagnostics, AIC/AICc/BIC. See Hyndman and Athanasopoulos (2021) for background.
